runAssessment.summary: The run produced the requested files but failed honestly before executing tests, probing the HTTP service, or delivering a result because the sole execution call ended with a provider error after 226 seconds. Total cost was $0.11706 over 329 seconds; most spend was in initial planning ($0.06618), while the failed execution cost $0.01448. There was no retry loop or false delivery claim, so the trace supports a provider-variance failure with unremarkable spend rather than an atoma defect.

findings.title: Provider error ended execution after file creation but before verification
findings.detail: Methane wrote package.json, server.js, test.js, and README.md, then its execution call failed with a provider error. No run_shell, server-start, HTTP probe, result validation, or delivery event followed, so implementation correctness and the tests' discriminatory coverage remain unverified.

findings.title: No recovery path was attempted after the execution provider error
findings.detail: The provider failure occurred after durable workspace writes, but the trace moved directly to branch closure without retrying or resuming verification. Whether and how to retry a stateful execution call after partial tool effects requires a policy decision about retry limits, workspace preservation, and duplicate side effects; this single run does not establish a broken existing contract.

Methane's plan received both mechanical and LLM validation before execution; no revision was required.

execution.summary: Methane found an empty workspace and wrote all four requested files, including a real subprocess-oriented test file. It redundantly rewrote package.json and server.js, but the execution then suffered a provider error before any command, server launch, or HTTP probe, leaving behavior unverified. validation.summary: Plan validation occurred and accepted the intended coverage, but result validation did not occur. The trace contains no observed npm test execution, subprocess startup, HTTP input/output assertion, persistence restart, or refusal-path observation, so neither the implementation nor the claimed test coverage can be treated as proven.

recovery.summary: There were no retries, fallbacks, escalations, or cancellation. After the first recorded provider error, both nested branches closed immediately; this avoided repetitive spend but abandoned potentially resumable work already written to disk.

learning.summary: The run matched and injected the existing build-persisted-json-api skill, and trusted Sclereid through its recorded success fast path. Because execution failed before validated delivery, the trajectory was not credited; no compilation or trust update is recorded.
